1480: They argued over the price like it was a stage play, then handed me far too much so I'd remember them.
1481: We haggled for an hour, very loudly. Then they paid triple and made sure I watched them do it.
1482: They bargained as if the whole town were watching, won, and then insisted on paying more than I asked.
1483: Such a performance over a few coins. Then they overpaid, bowed low, and asked if I'd remember the face.
1484: They fought me down to half price, then set the full amount back on the counter and added extra.
1485: The whole market gathered to watch them haggle. Then they overpaid, on purpose, and enjoyed the gasps.
1486: They clutched their chest at my price like it had wounded them, then paid double with a happy smile.
1487: We shook hands on a bargain. They tore up the bargain and paid me far more, just to be remembered.
1488: They haggled with great drama, lost cheerfully, and left me a pile of coins I hadn't actually earned.
1489: First they called my prices robbery. Then they paid above every one of them and looked very pleased.
1490: They negotiated like an actor, sighed like a mourner, and finished by overpaying and taking a bow.
1491: A grand show of counting every coin twice — then they simply left me twice as many as I asked.
1492: They begged for a discount, got it, refused it, and said the extra was so I would not forget them.
1493: Loudest haggler I've had. Then they overpaid, told me to keep the change, and asked my name for later.
1494: They spent ages disputing a single coin, then dropped a fistful more than the total and swept off.
1495: They made a scene over the price, won the argument, and then paid me the losing amount anyway.
1496: They bargained hard, then paid so much extra I tried to give it back. They refused, delighted.
1497: A great theatrical struggle over a single coin, ending with them overpaying and asking that I remember the face.
1498: They talked my price down, then paid me above where it started, and thanked the crowd for watching.
1499: They talked me into a lower price, then handed over the higher one twice and seemed proud of the loss.
1500: They gave me a gold coin to say nothing. It is a real coin. My silence, a little less so.
1501: A stranger pressed gold into my hand for my silence. The gold is true. The silence I'm still deciding.
1502: They paid me a shiny coin to forget their face. I bit it — real gold. My memory, though, is for sale.
1503: They gave me more money than I'd ever held, just to keep quiet. I'm quiet until someone pays more.
1504: They slipped me a gold coin and a wink. The coin bought a promise I'm not entirely sure I made.
1505: A rich stranger paid me to see nothing. I saw plenty. But the coin was real, so I'll allow that.
1506: They handed me gold to hush me up. I'm keeping the coin. The hush is available for the right offer.
1507: They thought a gold coin buys a boy's silence forever. It buys it for exactly as long as it lasts.
1508: Someone grand pressed a coin in my palm to keep me quiet. Quiet is my only trade, and it is open.
1509: They paid for my silence with real gold. Nobody told them a silence can quietly be sold again.
1510: A gold coin to look the other way. I looked. Then I looked back, since the coin never said how long.
1511: They gave me gold and said, 'You saw nothing.' I said nothing. But nothing is negotiable.
1512: The fanciest stranger I've met paid me to forget them. The coin's real. The forgetting is a rental.
1513: They bribed me with gold to keep still. I stayed still until the coin got lonely in my pocket.
1514: One gold coin for my silence. They forgot to ask whether I owned more than one silence to sell.
1515: They pressed gold into my hand for secrecy. Secrecy's my specialty — and it comes back to market.
1516: They gave me gold to say I never saw them. I never say I saw them. I only hint, for a small fee.
1517: They paid a street kid in real gold for quiet. The quiet, it turns out, has an expiry date.
1518: A whole gold coin to keep me quiet. I am very quiet. Whether I stay quiet costs a second coin.
1519: They bought my silence with gold. A fair trade — until a better buyer happens to wander by.
